transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in. What brings you in today?
I’ve felt this low, empty mood hanging over me for years now, like I can’t shake feeling down no matter what I do. It just feels like a constant weight that is always there in the background.
Have you ever had a period of at least 2 months when your mood felt normal or back to your usual self, or has this low mood been present most days for years without a break?

No, I haven't had any break from it at all. This heavy, low mood has been with me almost every single day for over three years now, ever since my divorce. I haven't had a single period where I felt back to my normal self during this whole time.
During these past three years, have you also had symptoms like low energy, poor self-esteem, trouble sleeping, poor appetite, or difficulty concentrating most days?

I’ve definitely struggled with severe low energy for those three years, feeling so wiped out after work that I don't even have the strength to cook or clean. I haven't really noticed any major issues with my sleep, appetite, or concentration, but this constant physical and mental exhaustion has been a major struggle.
During these years, have you also had low self-esteem, feelings of hopelessness, or trouble enjoying things you used to like?

I'm not really sure about low self-esteem, but I definitely feel a deep hopelessness, like things will never get better and this is just how my life is now. I've also lost all enjoyment in things I used to love, like hiking, cooking, and dancing, which now just feel like obligations I'm forcing myself to go through.

Have you ever had a distinct 2-week period during these years when your symptoms suddenly got much worse, with several new symptoms like markedly worse sadness, sleep or appetite changes, guilt, or trouble concentrating?

No, I haven't really noticed any specific two-week period where things suddenly got much worse or where I had those kinds of new symptoms. It has just been a steady, continuous low feeling that has stayed at about the same level for the past three years.

There is no history of a distinct major depressive episode or episodic worsening, supporting persistent depressive disorder (dysthymia).
